s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic abdominal pain and diarrhea with multi-organ involvement and granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Abdominal pain and loose, watery stools for 1.5 years
key_facts: 42-year-old man
1.5-year history of abdominal pain
Three loose, watery stools daily
Gastroesophageal reflux disease
Hereditary hemochromatosis (grade 3 iron overload, mild portal fibrosis, C282Y homozygosity)
No rectal bleeding, fever, or weight loss
Normal vital signs and unremarkable physical examination
Negative laboratory tests for ova and parasites, bacterial culture, fecal leukocytes, and Clostridium difficile NAAT
Negative Histoplasma antigen, anti-transglutaminase, and anti-endomysial antibodies
Erythematous mucosa in the transverse colon and rectum and congestion in the terminal ileum on colonoscopy
Diffuse gastric erythema with erosions and duodenitis on esophagogastroduodenoscopy
Non-caseating microgranulomas on biopsies from the stomach, duodenum, terminal ileum, colon, and rectum
Hepatosplenomegaly on CT of the abdomen and pelvis
Elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme level at 77 U/L

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme level and non-caseating microgranulomas on biopsies

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, and granulomatous inflammation on biopsies

shortlist.label: Whipple's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multi-organ involvement and granulomatous inflammation, although negative Tropheryma whipplei testing

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation, although negative laboratory tests for mycobacterial infection

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multi-organ involvement, granulomatous inflammation, and hepatosplenomegaly

raw.rationale: The presence of non-caseating microgranulomas on biopsies from multiple sites and an elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme level are highly suggestive of sarcoidosis, which is a systemic disease that can affect multiple organs, including the gastrointestinal tract and liver.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: While Crohn's disease can cause similar gastrointestinal symptoms, the presence of non-caseating microgranulomas and elevated ACE level are more characteristic of sarcoidosis.

rejected.label: Whipple's disease
rejected.why: Whipple's disease is a rare bacterial infection that typically presents with malabsorption, weight loss, and fever, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Tuberculosis
rejected.why: Tuberculosis typically presents with caseating granulomas, which were not found in this case.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
rejected.why: Erdheim-Chester disease is a rare histiocytic disorder that can cause granulomatous inflammation, but it is typically associated with other systemic symptoms and findings, such as bone pain and exophthalmos, which are not present in this case.
